feedback: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this review rests on the public contract and the baseline rationale only. Checked against the contract, the candidate is valid: all sensor positions, sensor_size 0.012, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body and mass, base_speed 1.6, kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] and line_loss last_direction are all inside their allowed ranges. Nothing looks obviously broken. The main open questions are whether base_speed 1.6 is fast enough to finish under 3.0 s (the course needs about 1.5 m/s average) and whether kp 3.0 with kd 0.3 is firm enough without causing oscillation. Those can only be answered by racing. This is early exploration with four review/revision actions left and eleven iterations after this one, so a valid baseline should race now to produce telemetry. After the race, read the results as follows. If completion is 0 or the run is cut short by line loss, raise kd and lower kp before changing speed. If completion is 1 but completion_time is above about 2.8 s and steering_oscillation is low, raise base_speed in steps of about 0.2. If steering_oscillation is high, lower kp by about 1.0 or raise kd by about 0.2 before touching base_speed. Keep sensor geometry fixed until the controller is stable.
requested_changes: If completion_time is above about 2.8 s with low steering_oscillation and completion = 1, raise controller.base_speed in steps of about 0.2 (for example 1.6 to 1.8), keeping the other fields unchanged.
If steering_oscillation is high or max_error is large on the slalom, reduce controller.kp by about 1.0 (3.0 to 2.0) or raise controller.kd by about 0.2 (0.3 to 0.5) to damp the response.
If line_loss_events is greater than 0 on any track, change controller.line_loss or widen the sensor spread (for example x = -0.03 to +0.03) so the tape stays under at least one sensor through bends.
